Per-evaluation cost: ~$0.20 low / ~$0.42 typical / ~$1.17 heavy, ~$0.45 blended; absolute per-eval ceiling ~$2.30 with all caps exhausted and caching working. Monthly: ~$45 @100, ~$450 @1,000, ~$4,500 @10,000 evaluations (platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing).

Verified rates (Aug 2026): Sonnet 5 (claude-sonnet-5) $2/$10 per MTok — the intro price is now permanent, the scheduled Sept 1 2026 increase to $3/$15 was cancelled; Haiku 4.5 (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001) $1/$5; cache read 0.1x, write 1.25x (5m) / 2x (1h); batch 50% off everything; web search $10/1,000 ($0.01/search); web fetch $0 fee, tokens only; no long-context surcharge on 4.6+ models.

S3 prompt caching is the single largest cost control: with cache_control set, the server-side loop auto-caches after each tool result and typical S3 costs $0.34; without it the same call is $0.74 typical and up to ~$6.40 worst-case. Monitor cache_read_input_tokens > 0 as a production invariant.

Search fees are only ~$0.12 of a typical eval — the volatile cost is tokens, and dynamic filtering (web_search_20260318 / web_fetch_20260318, free code execution, response_inclusion: 'excluded') is what tames it. Anthropic publishes no exact %; nearest published anchor is 24% input-token savings for the same filter-in-sandbox mechanism (programmatic tool calling).

Do NOT downgrade S3 to Haiku 4.5: it saves only ~15% ($0.36 vs $0.42 per eval) because Haiku lacks dynamic filtering (4.6+ models only) so raw results inflate its tokens ~60%, search fees don't scale down, and the heavy scenario's ~223K-token context exceeds Haiku's 200K window outright — the verification-hungry small-vendor cases literally cannot run.

Keep max_uses at 20 searches / 10 fetches: caps bind only on the ~10% heavy tail (typical evals use ~12 searches). If trimming is needed, cut max_content_tokens 30K→15K first (heavy S3 −17%, preserves number of independent sources) rather than halving max_uses (heavy −50% but degrades the customer-trace ladder — the fairness failure mode).
S6 chat budget: ~$0.006–0.007/turn on Haiku with the ~8.5K report context cached; recommend 10 turns x 800 max_tokens = ~$0.10 hard session ceiling, ~$0.03–0.07 typical session.

Design trap: Haiku 4.5's minimum cacheable prefix is 4,096 tokens — a shorter S5/S6 methodology prompt silently never caches (no error). Pad it to ≥4,096 tokens. TTL by volume: ≥~300 evals/day the 5-min cache self-sustains; below that use the 1-hour TTL (~$0.20–0.40/day total).

Abuse ceiling: a scripted actor at 1,000 junk evals/day burns $450–$2,300/day. Layered controls: Cloudflare Turnstile (free tier: 20 widgets, unlimited challenges), per-IP/session caps (3/day anonymous, 10/day verified .gov), vendor-keyed result caching (pitches concentrate in the same vendors — 30% repeat rate cuts the bill 30%), and a Console Workspace spend limit as hard backstop.

Bulk/queued triage through the Batches API runs at ~$0.26 per full eval (50% off all tokens, search fee unchanged, server-tool loop supported with a higher iteration limit, most batches <1 hour); use 1-hour cache TTL inside batches (hit rates are best-effort, 30–98%).

Flagged estimates to replace with measurements in week one (not documented anywhere): tokens per search-result block (modeled ~1.2K filtered / ~2.5–3K raw) and server-loop iteration count (modeled ~(searches+fetches)/2 + 2). Log response.usage per stage from day one.

Government caveat: dynamic-filtering tool versions are NOT Zero-Data-Retention-eligible (they ride on code execution); a ZDR requirement forces allowed_callers:['direct'] and roughly doubles S3 token cost.

Lifecycle risks: Haiku 4.5's retirement commitment runs only to 'not sooner than Oct 15, 2026' — budget a migration re-baseline within the tool's first year; Sonnet 5 pricing risk is resolved (permanent $2/$10).
Free-tier sizing: $500/month supports ~1,100 blended evaluations (~1,500 with a 30% vendor-repeat cache-hit rate); a $100/month pilot covers ~200–250.
